topics.title: Overview, Objectives & Key Definitions
topics.concept:
Unit Overview

This capstone unit puts the definite integral to work. You will compute average value, use integrals for motion (displacement and total distance), find areas between curves, and calculate volumes of solids — both by cross sections and by rotation (disk/washer, with shells as an extension). These are the classic "set up and evaluate an integral" problems that dominate AP free-response.

The skill is twofold: set up the correct integral (the hardest part) and evaluate it using Unit 6 techniques.

Big picture: Slice the region/solid into thin pieces, express each piece's measure as an integrand, and integrate to total it.

Learning Objectives

  • Compute the average value of a function and apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals.
  • Use integrals for rectilinear motion: displacement ∫v and total distance ∫|v|; recover position from velocity and velocity from acceleration.
  • Find area between curves, integrating with respect to x or y.
  • Find volumes with known cross sections (squares, semicircles, triangles).
  • Find volumes of revolution by the disk and washer methods (and shell method).

Prerequisite Concepts

  • Definite integrals and the FTC (Unit 6); u-substitution.
  • Geometry: areas of circles/triangles, volume intuition.
  • Finding intersection points of curves.

quiz.q: The average value of a function f on the interval [a, b] is given by:
options: (1/(b - a)) * integral from a to b of f(x) dx
integral from a to b of f(x) dx
quiz.explanation: The average value is the integral of f over [a, b] divided by the length of the interval: (1/(b - a)) integral from a to b of f dx.

topics.title: Important Theorems & Formulas
topics.concept:
Key Definitions & Formulas

Average value of f on [a, b]: f_avg = (1/(b − a)) ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx.

Motion:

  • Displacement on [a, b]: ∫ₐᵇ v(t) dt (net; can be negative).
  • Total distance on [a, b]: ∫ₐᵇ |v(t)| dt (split at v = 0).
  • Position: s(b) = s(a) + ∫ₐᵇ v(t) dt; velocity: v(t) = v(a) + ∫ₐᵗ a(τ) dτ.

Area between curves (top T, bottom B): ∫ₐᵇ [T(x) − B(x)] dx; or with horizontal strips ∫_c^d [R(y) − L(y)] dy (right − left).

Volume by cross sections with area A(x): V = ∫ₐᵇ A(x) dx. Common cross sections of "size" s:

  • Square: A = s²
  • Semicircle (diameter s): A = (π/8) s²
  • Equilateral triangle (side s): A = (√3/4) s²

Volume of revolution about the x-axis:

  • Disk: V = π ∫ₐᵇ [f(x)]² dx
  • Washer: V = π ∫ₐᵇ ([R(x)]² − [r(x)]²) dx

Shell method (about the y-axis): V = 2π ∫ₐᵇ x·f(x) dx.

Important Theorem

Mean Value Theorem for Integrals: If f is continuous on [a, b], there exists c in [a, b] with f(c) = f_avg — the function attains its average value at some point.

quiz.q: Find the average value of f(x) = x^2 on [0, 3].
quiz.explanation: Average = (1/3) integral from 0 to 3 of x^2 dx = (1/3)[x^3/3] from 0 to 3 = (1/3)(9) = 3.

quiz.q: Find the average value of f(x) = 2x on [1, 5].
quiz.explanation: Average = (1/4) integral from 1 to 5 of 2x dx = (1/4)[x^2] from 1 to 5 = (1/4)(25 - 1) = 24/4 = 6.

quiz.q: A particle has velocity v(t). The displacement from t = a to t = b is:
options: integral from a to b of v(t) dt
integral from a to b of |v(t)| dt
quiz.explanation: Displacement (net change in position) is the integral of velocity: integral from a to b of v(t) dt.

quiz.q: The total distance traveled by a particle from t = a to t = b is:
options: integral from a to b of |v(t)| dt
integral from a to b of v(t) dt
quiz.explanation: Total distance uses the absolute value of velocity (to count motion in both directions): integral from a to b of |v(t)| dt.

quiz.q: A particle moves with v(t) = 3t^2. Its displacement from t = 0 to t = 2 is:
quiz.explanation: Displacement = integral from 0 to 2 of 3t^2 dt = [t^3] from 0 to 2 = 8.

topics.title: Concept Explanations & Solved Examples
topics.concept:
Concept Explanations

Average value (8.1). The average value is the constant height of a rectangle on [a, b] with the same area as under f. It's an integral divided by length — not the average of the endpoints.

Motion via integrals (8.2). Integration reverses Unit 4's differentiation of motion. Displacement is the signed integral of velocity; total distance requires |v|, so find where v = 0 and integrate each piece with the correct sign. To recover position, add the accumulated displacement to the starting position.

Area between curves (8.3–8.4). Integrate (top − bottom) with respect to x, or (right − left) with respect to y. Choose the variable that avoids splitting the region: use dy (horizontal strips) when boundaries are naturally x = (function of y), as with y² = x.

Cross-section volumes (8.5, 8.7). The base region gives the size of each slice; the cross-section shape gives its area formula A(x). Integrate A(x) along the axis. For squares, A = side²; for semicircles, A = (π/8)(diameter)², etc.

Solids of revolution (8.6, 8.8). Rotating a region sweeps a solid. Disks (solid slice) use radius = distance to the axis; washers subtract an inner radius when there's a gap. The shell method integrates cylindrical shells 2π·(radius)(height) — handy for rotation about the y-axis when the curve is y = f(x).

Worked Examples

Example 1 (Average value). f(x) = x² on [0, 3]: f_avg = (1/3)∫₀³ x² dx = (1/3)(9) = 3.

Example 2 (Total distance). v(t) = t − 2 on [0, 3]: v = 0 at t = 2. Distance = ∫₀² (2 − t) dt + ∫₂³ (t − 2) dt = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5.

Example 3 (Area between curves). Between y = x² and y = 4: intersect at x = ±2, ∫₋₂² (4 − x²) dx = 32/3. (from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 4 (Area with dy). Bounded by y² = x and y = x − 2: intersect at y = −1, 2. ∫₋₁² [(y + 2) − y²] dy = 10/3. (from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 5 (Disk). Rotate y = x³ on [0, 1] about the x-axis: V = π∫₀¹ x⁶ dx = π/7. (from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 6 (Sphere via disks). Rotate y = √(a² − x²) on [−a, a]: V = π∫₋ₐᵃ (a² − x²) dx = (4/3)πa³. (from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 7 (Washer). Between y = x (outer) and y = x² (inner) on [0, 1] about the x-axis: V = π∫₀¹ (x² − x⁴) dx = 2π/15.

Example 8 (Cross sections). Base under y = 4 − x², square cross sections of side (4 − x²): V = ∫₋₂² (4 − x²)² dx.

quiz.q: If a particle has acceleration a(t) = 6t and v(0) = 0, what is v(t)?
quiz.explanation: v(t) = integral of 6t dt = 3t^2 + C. Using v(0) = 0 gives C = 0, so v(t) = 3t^2.

quiz.q: The area between two curves y = f(x) (top) and y = g(x) (bottom) from x = a to x = b is:
options: integral from a to b of [f(x) - g(x)] dx
integral from a to b of [g(x) - f(x)] dx
integral from a to b of f(x) g(x) dx
quiz.explanation: The area between curves is the integral of (top curve minus bottom curve): integral from a to b of [f(x) - g(x)] dx.

quiz.q: Find the area of the region enclosed between y = x^2 and the line y = 4.
quiz.explanation: The curves meet at x = -2 and x = 2. Area = integral from -2 to 2 of (4 - x^2) dx = [4x - x^3/3] from -2 to 2 = (8 - 8/3) - (-8 + 8/3) = 32/3. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

quiz.q: Find the area between y = x and y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 1.
quiz.explanation: On [0, 1], x >= x^2. Area = integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2) dx = [x^2/2 - x^3/3] from 0 to 1 = 1/2 - 1/3 = 1/6.

quiz.q: When is it easier to integrate with respect to y (using horizontal strips) to find an area?
options: when the curves are given as x in terms of y, or a single top/bottom is hard to identify
quiz.explanation: Integrating with respect to y is convenient when boundaries are naturally expressed as x = (function of y), avoiding splitting the region.

topics.title: Graphical Interpretation, Common Mistakes & Tips
topics.concept:
Graphical Interpretation

  • Area between curves is the region trapped between two graphs; a thin vertical strip has height (top − bottom).
  • A disk/washer is what a vertical strip sweeps out when rotated — a circular slab of radius = distance to the axis.
  • A shell is what a strip parallel to the axis sweeps — a thin cylinder of radius x and height f(x).

Common Mistakes

  • Average of endpoints instead of the integral formula for average value.
  • Using v instead of |v| for total distance (missing the split at v = 0).
  • Top − bottom reversed, producing a negative area.
  • Forgetting to square the radius in disk/washer (π∫R², not π∫R), or subtracting radii instead of their squares in the washer (R² − r², not (R − r)²).
  • Wrong cross-section area formula (e.g., using r² instead of the semicircle's (π/8)s²).
  • Mismatching the variable of integration with the strip orientation.

AP Exam Tips

  • These are free-response staples — practice writing the integral set-up cleanly; a correct unevaluated integral earns significant credit.
  • Always find intersection points first to get the limits of integration.
  • For distance vs. displacement, state where v = 0 and split accordingly.
  • Label the radius/height clearly for volume problems; for washers, identify outer vs. inner radius.
  • On calculator-active questions, set up the integral by hand, then evaluate numerically.

Unit Summary

  • Average value: (1/(b − a))∫ₐᵇ f.
  • Motion: displacement ∫v; total distance ∫|v| (split at v = 0); position = s(a) + ∫v.
  • Area: ∫(top − bottom) dx or ∫(right − left) dy.
  • Volumes: cross sections ∫A(x) dx; disk π∫R²; washer π∫(R² − r²); shell 2π∫x·f(x).
  • The universal method: slice → integrand → integrate.

This completes AP Calculus AB. Together, Units 1–8 build from limits to derivatives to integrals and their applications — the full arc of single-variable calculus tested on the AP exam.

quiz.q: Find the average value of f(x) = sin(x) on [0, pi].
quiz.explanation: Average = (1/pi) integral from 0 to pi of sin(x) dx = (1/pi)[-cos(x)] from 0 to pi = (1/pi)(1 + 1) = 2/pi.

quiz.q: By the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals, if the average value of f on [a, b] is 5, then there is a c in [a, b] with:
quiz.explanation: The MVT for Integrals guarantees a point c where f(c) equals the average value of f on the interval.

quiz.q: A particle has velocity v(t) = t - 2 (m/s). What is the total distance traveled from t = 0 to t = 3?
quiz.explanation: v = 0 at t = 2. Distance = integral from 0 to 2 of |t - 2| dt + integral from 2 to 3 of (t - 2) dt = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 m. (Each piece is a triangle: area 2 and area 0.5.)

quiz.q: A particle starts at position s(0) = 5 with velocity v(t) = 2t. Its position at t = 3 is:
quiz.explanation: s(3) = s(0) + integral from 0 to 3 of 2t dt = 5 + [t^2] from 0 to 3 = 5 + 9 = 14.

quiz.q: Find the area of the region bounded by y = sin(x) and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 2pi (total area).
quiz.explanation: Sine is positive on [0, pi] (area 2) and negative on [pi, 2pi] (area 2). Total area = 2 + 2 = 4. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

mock_tests.title: Practice Set A

questions.q: The area bounded by x = y^2 and x = 4 (integrating with respect to y) is:
questions.explanation: The curves meet at y = -2 and y = 2. Area = integral from -2 to 2 of (4 - y^2) dy = [4y - y^3/3] from -2 to 2 = 32/3.

questions.q: A solid has a base region and square cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis with side length s(x). Its volume is:
questions.explanation: For square cross sections, the cross-sectional area is s(x)^2, so the volume is the integral of s(x)^2 over the base interval.

questions.q: By the Disk Method, rotating the region under y = f(x) on [a, b] about the x-axis gives volume:
options: pi integral from a to b of [f(x)]^2 dx
integral from a to b of [f(x)]^2 dx
2 pi integral from a to b of f(x) dx
pi integral from a to b of f(x) dx
questions.explanation: Each disk has radius f(x) and area pi[f(x)]^2, so V = pi integral from a to b of [f(x)]^2 dx.

questions.q: By the Washer Method, rotating the region between y = R(x) (outer) and y = r(x) (inner) about the x-axis gives:
questions.explanation: A washer's area is pi(R^2 - r^2), so the volume is pi integral of ([R(x)]^2 - [r(x)]^2) dx.

questions.q: For a solid where the cross-sectional area is given by A(x), the volume over [a, b] is:
options: integral from a to b of A(x) dx
pi integral from a to b of A(x) dx
integral from a to b of [A(x)]^2 dx
questions.explanation: Volume by known cross sections is the integral of the cross-sectional area function: integral from a to b of A(x) dx.

questions.q: A solid's cross-sectional area is A(x) = 4x. What is its volume from x = 0 to x = 3?
questions.explanation: V = integral from 0 to 3 of 4x dx = [2x^2] from 0 to 3 = 18.

questions.q: By the Shell Method, rotating the region under y = f(x) on [a, b] about the y-axis gives volume:
options: 2 pi integral from a to b of x f(x) dx
pi integral from a to b of [f(x)]^2 dx
2 pi integral from a to b of f(x) dx
pi integral from a to b of x f(x) dx
questions.explanation: A cylindrical shell has radius x, height f(x), and thickness dx, so its volume element is 2 pi x f(x) dx; V = 2 pi integral from a to b of x f(x) dx.

questions.q: Find the average value of f(x) = 3x^2 on [0, 2].
questions.explanation: Average = (1/2) integral from 0 to 2 of 3x^2 dx = (1/2)[x^3] from 0 to 2 = (1/2)(8) = 4.

questions.q: Find the area between y = x^2 and y = x from x = 0 to x = 1.
questions.explanation: On [0, 1], x >= x^2. Area = integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2) dx = 1/2 - 1/3 = 1/6.

questions.q: Rotate the region under y = 2 (a constant) on [0, 3] about the x-axis. The volume (a cylinder) is:
questions.explanation: V = pi integral from 0 to 3 of (2)^2 dx = pi(4)(3) = 12pi (a cylinder of radius 2 and height 3).

questions.q: A car's velocity is v(t) = 60 (constant, mph) for 2 hours. The distance traveled is:
questions.explanation: Distance = integral from 0 to 2 of 60 dt = 60(2) = 120 miles.

questions.q: The region bounded by x = y^2 and x = y + 2 is most naturally integrated:
questions.explanation: Since both boundaries are given as x in terms of y, integrating with respect to y (horizontal strips) is most direct.

questions.q: Rotating the region under y = x from x = 0 to x = 3 about the x-axis produces a cone with volume:
questions.explanation: V = pi integral from 0 to 3 of x^2 dx = pi[x^3/3] from 0 to 3 = pi(9) = 9pi.

questions.q: The average value of a constant function f(x) = 7 on any interval is:
questions.explanation: The average value of a constant is the constant itself: 7.

questions.q: A particle's acceleration is a(t) = 2, with v(0) = 1 and s(0) = 0. Its position at t = 2 is:
Find the area between y = 4 - x^2 and the x-axis.
questions.explanation: The parabola meets the x-axis at x = -2 and x = 2. Area = integral from -2 to 2 of (4 - x^2) dx = [4x - x^3/3] from -2 to 2 = 32/3.

questions.q: Rotating the region under y = f(x) about the x-axis, the radius of each disk equals:
questions.explanation: For rotation about the x-axis, the disk's radius is the distance from the axis to the curve, which is f(x).

questions.q: The Shell Method is most convenient when rotating a region about the y-axis and the region is described by:
options: y as a function of x
x as a function of y only
questions.explanation: Shells (radius x, height f(x)) work naturally when the curve is y = f(x) and rotation is about the y-axis, avoiding solving for x.

questions.q: For a solid with circular (disk) cross sections of radius r(x), the cross-sectional area is:
questions.explanation: A circle of radius r(x) has area pi[r(x)]^2.

questions.q: The average value of f(x) = x on [0, 4] is:
questions.explanation: Average = (1/4) integral from 0 to 4 of x dx = (1/4)[x^2/2] from 0 to 4 = (1/4)(8) = 2.

mock_tests.title: Practice Set B

questions.q: The area of a region bounded on the left by x = g(y) and on the right by x = f(y) from y = c to y = d is:
options: integral from c to d of [f(y) - g(y)] dy
integral from c to d of [g(y) - f(y)] dy
integral from c to d of f(y) g(y) dy
questions.explanation: Using horizontal strips, area = integral of (right curve minus left curve) with respect to y: integral from c to d of [f(y) - g(y)] dy.

questions.q: If a solid's cross-sectional area is A(x) = x^2 on [0, 2], its volume is:
questions.explanation: V = integral from 0 to 2 of x^2 dx = [x^3/3] from 0 to 2 = 8/3.

questions.q: Find the area under y = 1/x from x = 1 to x = e.
questions.explanation: Area = integral from 1 to e of (1/x) dx = [ln x] from 1 to e = ln(e) - ln(1) = 1.

questions.q: A particle has v(t) = 4t - t^2. On [0, 4], the velocity is nonnegative, so the total distance equals:
questions.explanation: Since v >= 0 on [0, 4], distance = integral from 0 to 4 of (4t - t^2) dt = [2t^2 - t^3/3] from 0 to 4 = 32 - 64/3 = 32/3.

questions.q: The volume of a solid with square cross sections is found by integrating:
options: the area (side)^2 of each square along the axis
questions.explanation: Volume by cross sections integrates the cross-sectional area; for squares that area is side^2.

questions.q: Find the area bounded by x = y^2 and x = 4 (with respect to y).
questions.explanation: Meets at y = -2 and y = 2. Area = integral from -2 to 2 of (4 - y^2) dy = [4y - y^3/3] from -2 to 2 = 32/3.

questions.q: Rotating the region under y = x + 1 on [0, 2] about the x-axis, the disk radius at position x is:
questions.explanation: For rotation about the x-axis, the radius equals the function value, x + 1.

questions.q: The average value of f(x) = 4 - x on [0, 4] is:
questions.explanation: Average = (1/4) integral from 0 to 4 of (4 - x) dx = (1/4)[4x - x^2/2] from 0 to 4 = (1/4)(16 - 8) = 2.

questions.q: Find the area between the curves y = sin(x) and y = cos(x) from x = 0 to their first intersection at x = pi/4.
questions.explanation: On [0, pi/4], cos(x) >= sin(x). Area = integral from 0 to pi/4 of (cos x - sin x) dx = [sin x + cos x] from 0 to pi/4 = (sqrt(2)) - (1) = sqrt(2) - 1. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by y = e^x, y = e^(-x), and the vertical line x = 1.
questions.explanation: For x in [0, 1], e^x >= e^(-x). Area = integral from 0 to 1 of (e^x - e^(-x)) dx = [e^x + e^(-x)] from 0 to 1 = (e + e^(-1)) - (1 + 1) = e + e^(-1) - 2. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola y^2 = x and the line y = x - 2 (integrating with respect to y).
questions.explanation: The curves meet at y = -1 and y = 2 (x = y^2 and x = y + 2). Area = integral from -1 to 2 of [(y + 2) - y^2] dy = [y^2/2 + 2y - y^3/3] from -1 to 2 = 10/3. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Find the area bounded by y = ln(x), y = 0, and x = e (using the region under the curve).
questions.explanation: Area = integral from 1 to e of ln(x) dx = [x ln x - x] from 1 to e = (e - e) - (0 - 1) = 1. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: A solid has a base bounded by y = x and y = x^2 on [0, 1], with square cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis. Which integral gives the volume?
options: integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2)^2 dx
integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2) dx
pi integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2)^2 dx
integral from 0 to 1 of (x^2 - x)^2 dx * 2
questions.explanation: The side of each square equals the vertical distance between the curves, (x - x^2). The area is (x - x^2)^2, so V = integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^2)^2 dx.

questions.q: A solid has semicircular cross sections (diameter = height of the region) perpendicular to the x-axis, with region height h(x). The cross-sectional area is:
questions.explanation: A semicircle with diameter h(x) has radius h(x)/2. Area = (1/2)pi r^2 = (1/2)pi(h/2)^2 = (pi/8) h^2.

questions.q: Find the volume of the solid generated by rotating the region under y = x^3 on [0, 1] about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: V = pi integral from 0 to 1 of (x^3)^2 dx = pi integral from 0 to 1 of x^6 dx = pi[x^7/7] from 0 to 1 = pi/7. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Find the volume when the region under y = sqrt(a^2 - x^2) from x = -a to x = a is rotated about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: V = pi integral from -a to a of (a^2 - x^2) dx = pi[a^2 x - x^3/3] from -a to a = (4/3)pi a^3 (the volume of a sphere of radius a). (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Find the volume when the region bounded by y = 2x - x^2 and the x-axis is rotated about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: The region spans x = 0 to x = 2. V = pi integral from 0 to 2 of (2x - x^2)^2 dx = pi integral of (4x^2 - 4x^3 + x^4) dx = pi[4x^3/3 - x^4 + x^5/5] from 0 to 2 = 16pi/15. (Adapted from the Vidaara NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Rotate the region between y = x and y = x^2 on [0, 1] about the x-axis. The volume is:
questions.explanation: Outer radius x, inner x^2. V = pi integral from 0 to 1 of (x^2 - x^4) dx = pi[x^3/3 - x^5/5] from 0 to 1 = pi(1/3 - 1/5) = pi(2/15) = 2pi/15.

questions.q: A solid has a base that is the region under y = 4 - x^2 (x from -2 to 2, y >= 0) and equilateral-triangle cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis with side (4 - x^2). The area of each cross section is:
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle of side s has area (sqrt(3)/4)s^2. With s = 4 - x^2, the area is (sqrt(3)/4)(4 - x^2)^2.

questions.q: Using the Shell Method, find the volume when the region under y = x on [0, 2] is rotated about the y-axis.
questions.explanation: V = 2 pi integral from 0 to 2 of x(x) dx = 2 pi integral from 0 to 2 of x^2 dx = 2 pi[x^3/3] from 0 to 2 = 2 pi(8/3) = 16pi/3.
